reports.title: Williams-Sonoma, Inc. announces strong third quarter 2026 results

guidance.heading: OUTLOOK
section: •In fiscal 2026, we expect annual net revenues in the range of +4.7% to +7.2%, with comps in the range of +4.0% to +6.5%; and an operating margin, on a non-GAAP basis, between 17.8% to 18.2%.
•For fiscal 2026, we expect annual interest income of approximately $30 million and an effective tax rate of approximately 26%, both on a non-GAAP basis.
•Looking beyond fiscal 2026, we remain confident in our growth strategies and operational execution and will provide guidance for fiscal 2027 in March per our usual cadence.

desk.headline: Sales up 5.8% to $2.0bn, a touch below estimates; adjusted EPS $2.19 just short; full-year outlook reiterated

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (non-GAAP) diluted; excludes tariff refund income

results: Net revenue rose 5.8% to $2.0bn and comparable brand revenue rose 5.1%, with every brand and channel positive.
West Elm (+7.0% comp) and Williams Sonoma (+6.8%) led; Pottery Barn grew a slower 1.8%.
Adjusted EPS rose 11.7% to $2.19; GAAP EPS was $2.38 after a $29.3m one-off tariff refund.
Adjusted gross margin edged up to 46.2%; higher oil-driven supply chain costs took 0.5 pts off it.
Cash of $992m; $253m returned in the quarter through buybacks and dividends. Inventory up 7.3% to $1.64bn.

guidance.summary: Williams-Sonoma repeated its fiscal 2026 outlook: sales growth of 4.7% to 7.2% and an adjusted operating margin of 17.8% to 18.2%. Fiscal 2027 guidance comes in March.

points: Diesel prices up more than 60% y/y cost about 0.75 pts of margin in Q3; up to $60m extra diesel cost expected for the year.
Fewer promotions and shallower markdowns to lift full-price selling, including over the holidays, even at some cost to near-term growth.
Online comps rose 6.8% and business-to-business sales 15%; store comps rose 1.5%.
No more tariff refunds expected in Q4; management said the housing market weakened during the quarter.
Port congestion and longer transit times may delay some holiday deliveries; long-term targets said to be unchanged.
call.source: Call coverage: MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance and Investing.com, 19 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Whether diesel and shipping costs push the full-year margin toward the low end of 17.8%–18.2%.
Holiday sales with fewer markdowns, and any further housing-market weakness.
